newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen higher at start. [CORRECTED 01:25 GMT 10/4]
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen higher at start. [CORRECTED 01:25 GMT 10/4]

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to head higher at the start of trading, extending the bounce of the last three days.
Merger activity continues, with Procter & Gamble Co's announcement that it will acquire Tambrands Inc for $50 per share, or $1.85 billion.

"I think we will have a fairly positive day," said Hildergard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities. "We have had three up sessions, and bonds are steady. There is nothing to put a damper on today. There are no numbers coming out."
Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said the P&G/Tambrands deal, coming on the heels of several other merger announcements this week, was good news for the market.

"When you see mergers and takeovers, it tells you that corporate America remains confident that the economy will do well, interest rates will not skyrocket and we are not heading for a recession," he said. "The more mergers we see, the more confidence it builds."
The Standard & Poor's 500 index futures contract for June was up 1.15 at 773.20.
In Tokyo the Nikkei Average was down (corrects from up) 318.33 points, or 1.77 percent, at 17,703.37.
In London the FTSE 100 index was up 23.7 points at 4293.0.
Among U.S. shares traded in London, International Business Machines Corp was down 1/4 at 136-3/8 while Digital Equipment Corp added 1/4 to 27. P&G was up 1/4 to 116-1/8.
The dollar was firmer but stalled below earlier highs in Tokyo. It was steady in Europe after shedding some gains.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly higher, with the long bond up 7/32 to yield 7.08 percent.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column said office furniture maker Knoll still plans to go public despite the uncertain market, hoping to raise $160 million or so early in May.

The New York Times's Market Place column said the volume and prices of Alex. Brown Inc shares and options soared before its announced merger with Bankers Trust New York Corp. It also said Tambrands was soaring in stock and options markets.
